neighbours.label: the end of a sentence-opening set-up phrase that looks back at what came before ('Now that we've …,' 'Once you're …,' 'Despite this … beginning'), just before the main clause
fire: That covers the basic tools, though there are many more. Now that we've sorted out the kit, let's talk about technique.
The first week is the hardest part. Once you're past that hump, everything gets easier.
The two leaders shook hands warmly in March. Despite this hopeful start to the talks, the deal collapsed by summer.
The builders let the class watch from the fence. After several trips to the yard, the pupils started drawing cranes.
People warn you about the paperwork. Once you've joined the team, nobody mentions it again.
We hope those examples gave you a few ideas. Now that we've broken the ice, tell us about your own garden.
The opening concert sold out in an hour. In spite of this strong opening to the season, ticket sales soon dropped.
The manual explains the menus in detail. Once you've learned the shortcuts, you rarely open it.

The manual explains the menus in detail. You rarely open it in practice.
